title: Lior and the Wolf
premise: Jonah Thackeray, a smuggler and bone-carver who hears the voices of the dead in his carvings, takes in Lior, a mute child who speaks only in a language older than any living kingdom. The dead tell Jonah that Lior is the last heir of Vaelthorne, a country erased from maps and memory by dragon-fire two centuries ago, and that she alone can open its final door before the last ember of its guardian dragon gutters out forever. Hunted by the Ashen Order, who erased Vaelthorne and will kill to keep it erased, Jonah and Lior cross the Thornfell mountains along roads the dead remember but the living have forgotten. At the door of vanished Vaelthorne, Jonah must choose between sealing himself inside a dead nation with the voices he loves or letting Lior walk through alone into a restored homeland he can never enter; he lets her go, and in doing so finally silences the dead and finds his own belonging among the living.
about_author: Juniper Hartwell is a former cartographer's apprentice from the Welsh borders who spent a decade collecting half-remembered place names from dying villages. She writes fantasy about countries that exist only in the mouths of the old.

chapters.title: The Bone-Carver's Quiet
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. In his workshop above the smuggler's road, Jonah carves a sparrow bone and hears its dead owner's last song. Establishes his gift as both comfort and curse: the dead never stop talking, and he has no one living to talk to. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: A Knock at Dusk
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A starving girl appears at his door during a snowstorm, speaking words no living tongue knows. When she touches his finished carvings, the dead go silent for the first time in thirty years. Emotional beat: wonder cracking open a closed life.

chapters.title: What the Sparrow Knew
chapters.summary: Lior's POV (rendered through sensation and image). Lior remembers fire, a white door, and a voice calling her 'the last.' She does not understand this world of roads and coins. Emotional beat: displacement, grief without vocabulary.

chapters.title: The Ashen Order Rides
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV. Inquisitor Serane Voss interrogates a village priest about rumors of a child speaking Old Vaelthorni. We learn the Order burned Vaelthorne from history itself, unmaking records, names, even memories. Emotional beat: cold institutional dread.

chapters.title: The Dead Give Directions
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A carved wolf femur speaks with an ancient voice: Lior is Vaelthorne's heir, and the door out of the dead country opens only while the last dragon-fire burns. The dead beg Jonah to take her home. Emotional beat: duty arriving unwanted.

chapters.title: Thief's Road
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He and Lior flee into the Thornfell mountains on smuggler paths only he knows. First bond forms: she teaches him her language's word for 'wolf,' which sounds like his name. Emotional beat: reluctant partnership warming.

chapters.title: The Village That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. They find a valley where a Vaelthorni village should be—empty fields, a well with no name. Lior grieves a home she barely remembers; Jonah realizes the erasure took the land too. Emotional beat: mourning made geographic.

chapters.title: Serane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. She tracks them using a ledger of unmade things, sensing where history 'itches.' Flashback reveals she was born in Vaelthorne and chose the Order to survive. Emotional beat: the antagonist as a wound that chose to scar over.

chapters.title: Wolves at the Ford
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Real wolves—and Order scouts dressed as hunters—corner them at a river crossing. Lior speaks a command in Old Vaelthorni and the true wolves turn aside, sparing the humans too. Emotional beat: first proof Lior's blood carries power.

chapters.title: The Ember Shrine
chapters.summary: Dual POV. In a mountain cave shrine, a single dragon-scale still glows—the last guttering flame. It shows Lior visions of the door and warns it dies within a season. Jonah hears the dead of Vaelthorne singing through it. Emotional beat: hope with a deadline.

chapters.title: Bargains with Bandits
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. To cross the Order's checkpoint gorge, Jonah bargains with his old smuggling crew, spending every favor and coin he has. His old partner Bram demands to know why one mute girl matters. Emotional beat: the cost of caring, paid publicly.

chapters.title: First Words
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. On a quiet night, Lior speaks her first Common Tongue words: 'Don't leave.' Jonah promises nothing, because everyone he's promised anything to is dead. Emotional beat: love against the fear of loss.

chapters.title: The Unmaking
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. The Order performs an Unmaking rite on a town that sheltered the pair, deleting it from memory mid-scene. Serane falters when a child's face in the crowd mirrors her own erased past. Emotional beat: cracks in conviction.

chapters.title: Betrayal at High Camp
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Bram, bought by the Order, sells their location. Scouts attack the high camp; Jonah is wounded holding the pass so Lior can run. Emotional beat: betrayal, sacrifice, and the terror of being separated.

chapters.title: Alone Above the Snowline
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lost and alone, Lior follows voices only she can hear now—the dead of Vaelthorne guiding her upward. She stops being a passenger and becomes the one who knows the way. Emotional beat: coming into her own inheritance.

chapters.title: The Wolf's Choice
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Captured by Serane, Jonah bargains with the only thing he has: the truth that Serane was born Vaelthorni, proven by a bone carving that sings her mother's lullaby. Emotional beat: weaponized compassion; identity as a blade.

chapters.title: What Serane Burned
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. Shaken, Serane lets Jonah go—or follows him secretly, torn between orders and the lullaby. She recalls the night she denounced her own family to survive the purge. Emotional beat: antagonist confronting what she traded away.

chapters.title: The Door of Vaelthorne
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Jonah and Lior reunite at the white door beneath the dying ember-shrine. The door opens only for the heir—but the dead warn that whoever enters belongs wholly to Vaelthorne, and cannot return. Emotional beat: the choice crystallized.

chapters.title: Ash and Ember
chapters.summary: Climax, dual POV. Serane arrives with the Order; battle erupts at the threshold as the last dragon-fire flares. Lior offers Serane entry—a home, a name restored. Serane turns on the Order instead, buying time with her life. Emotional beat: redemption purchased at the highest price.

chapters.title: The Last Door Out
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The door stands open; the ember dims to nothing. Jonah realizes entering means becoming one of the voices he's always heard—belonging, but as a ghost. Lior begs him to come. Emotional beat: love against duty, fully bared.

chapters.title: Let Her Go
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah stays on the threshold and pushes Lior gently through as the door seals. For the first time, the dead fall silent—not gone, but at peace, their country alive again beyond the seal. Emotional beat: grief transfigured into release.

chapters.title: The Carver Who Hears Nothing
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Jonah's POV. Seasons later, Jonah carves bones that hold only silence, and finds he can bear the quiet. On his doorstep each spring, small offerings appear in Old Vaelthorni script—from a country that exists again, remembering him. Emotional beat: belonging found not behind the door, but beside it.
